subject: Renewal discussion: hybrid annual prepay + credit bank structure
messages:
From: Jordan Miles <jmiles@featurelabs.io>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal & structure idea: hybrid annual prepay + credit bank

Rachel —

Our renewal window opens next quarter and procurement asked me to surface a model that locks current rates while giving us flexibility on consumption. Rather than a straight multi-year prepay, would Redwood entertain a hybrid annual prepay + "credit bank" model? High level: FeatureLabs prepays annual committed spend (locks price for 12 months) but we maintain a drawdown-style credit pool that can be used to smooth usage spikes; unused credits can carry forward on a capped basis.

Why this matters: we want price certainty (avoid the expected market step-up) but also avoid over-committing to a large multi-year prepay given uncertain growth. If there's a middle ground with staged annual prepays + carryover credits, that's attractive.

Would love a short call next week to run numbers and discuss how Redwood would treat credits (expiry, true-up, burst preservation, SLA for reserved capacity). Happy to share our expected monthly profile if helpful.

-Jordan
Jordan Miles
Head of Platform Ops, FeatureLabs
jmiles@featurelabs.io
+1 415-555-0199

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miles <jmiles@featurelabs.io>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal & structure idea: hybrid annual prepay + credit bank

Jordan — thanks for the clear framing and the proposed tradeoff. We can definitely model a hybrid approach. A few quick clarifying points before we sync: 

- Credit bank mechanics: we typically support annual credits that can be drawn down for burst above committed throughput; we can allow limited carryover (we usually cap carryover at 20% of the annual commitment). Would that be sufficient?
- True-up cadence: we recommend quarterly true-ups to reconcile consumption vs commit — keeps finance clean while avoiding large year-end adjustments.
- Pricing guardrails: we can lock the per-token rate for committed units for the year; usage above the commitment draws from credits at the same locked rate until credits exhaust, afterwards on-demand rates apply.
- Reserved capacity: if you need guaranteed latency for burst windows, we can add a small reserved pool (billed as part of the commit) to cover predictable peaks.

Aditya / Vivek / Laura: can you run two scenarios for FeatureLabs: (A) 1-year rolling annual prepay with 20% carryover and quarterly true-up; (B) 2-year laddered prepay (50% Year 1, 75% Year 2 commitment) with a 10% credit buffer. Please include cost delta vs pure on-demand, suggested reserved pool size for a 95th percentile spike, and any SLA implications. Jordan — once we have the numbers we'll share a draft term sheet and proposed legal/ops language for credits/expiry.

Thanks — R

Rachel Kim
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal & structure idea: hybrid annual prepay + credit bank

Looping in my notes from the scoping run — attaching the scenario workbook.

Attachment: prepay-model-scenario.xlsx (xlsx)

Quick takeaways:
- Scenario A (1y rolling + 20% carry): preserves most upside for FeatureLabs and gives them monthly flexibility; reduces their blended unit cost by ~18% vs on-demand if actual usage matches forecast within +/-15%.
- Scenario B (2y laddered): deeper discount (approx 25% blended) but client takes more volume risk; commit phasing helps their cash flow.
- Reserved pool: given their 95th spike profile, recommend a reserved cushion equal to ~7% of monthly peak to meet latency SLOs without material cost inflation.

Operational considerations for legal/ops language (Vivek / Laura to comment):
- Define carryover cap and expiry (recommend carryover credits expire 12 months after the year they were issued).
- True-up invoicing cadence and proration rules.
- Treatment for churn/downgrades mid-term (pro-rate and re-benchmark monthly usage).

Vivek: can you draft the operational language around reserved pool fallback and the automatic fallback to on-demand when credits deplete? Laura: finance will want the billing timelines/DocuSign flow — I sketched a DocuSign placeholder on the drive.

- Aditya

From: Jordan Miles <jmiles@featurelabs.io>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: FeatureLabs Procurement <procurement@featurelabs.io>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal & structure idea: hybrid annual prepay + credit bank

Rachel / team — this looks promising, thanks. The scenarios help a lot. A couple of operational asks from procurement: 

1) Can the carryover cap be increased to 25% for the first year only (we have some lumpy product launches planned)?
2) We want a one-time "swingline" credit option: if we exhaust credits in a month, a small overdraft (paid at the same locked rate + fixed fee) would prevent immediate throttling. Is that acceptable?

If you can reflect these two options in the term sheet (and include a non-binding DocuSign LOI link), we'll route to our CFO for quick sign-off. Happy to hop on a 30m call if easier.

Link: https://www.docusign.com/ABC-123

-Jordan
